headline: Record King Tides plus a big incoming swell bring moderate to major coastal flooding through Friday morning, locally extreme at Thursday morning's high tide, while inland it turns warm and gusty for Thanksgiving; showers are possible Sunday night into Monday and a stronger, possibly soaking storm may arrive around next Tuesday and Wednesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: High clouds from a storm passing to the north spread over the area Wednesday, then clear Wednesday night. Highs stay about the same as Tuesday, mostly in the 70s along the coast and in the valleys, with the mid to upper 70s in inland coastal spots and the western valleys. Northeast winds start picking up around 4 to 5 PM Wednesday below the mountain passes, with gusts of roughly 30 to 40 mph there.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: High pressure overhead and dry winds blowing out from the interior (offshore flow) bring warming for Thanksgiving and Friday, with northeast to east winds gusting 35 to 45 mph along and below the coastal slopes of the mountains. Thanksgiving highs climb 4 to 8 degrees, reaching the low to mid 80s in inland coastal areas and the western valleys, as much as 12 to 18 degrees above average, with little change Friday. The mountains and high desert warm about another 5 degrees on Friday, and high clouds increase again Friday night.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: High pressure weakens Saturday and the cooler ocean breeze returns, dropping coast and valley highs 4 to 8 degrees to the mid 70s to around 80, with steady cooling through Tuesday to the mid 60s in the far inland valleys and around 70 at the coast. A fast-moving storm crossing California Sunday brings a chance of showers Sunday night and Monday. A stormier pattern may follow, with a storm around Tuesday and Wednesday that could bring strong winds and heavy rain: from Tuesday morning through Thursday night the chance of 1 inch or more from the coast to the mountains is 75 to 85 percent in Orange and southwestern San Bernardino counties and about 60 percent in southern San Diego County, while the chance of 3 inches or more is 5 to 10 percent near the coast and 25 to 35 percent in the mountains.

coast: Morning high tides through Thursday are forecast at 7.9 to 8.3 feet, highest Wednesday morning; they run 1.1 to 1.2 feet above normal predictions and will likely break the all-time records set in late October. Surf of 3 to 5 feet Wednesday morning builds as a long-period west swell (7 to 8 feet every 16 to 18 seconds) arrives late Wednesday afternoon, producing 6 to 8 foot breakers Thursday with 10 to 12 foot sets on exposed west-facing beaches, then 3 to 7 feet Friday; a High Surf Advisory covers San Diego County beaches from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM Friday. The record tides plus big surf bring moderate to major coastal flooding, locally extreme at Thursday morning's high tide, under a Coastal Flood Warning for the Orange and San Diego County coasts until 1 PM Friday. Offshore, combined seas of 8 to 12 feet and northwest gusts near 20 knots in the far outer waters Wednesday afternoon bring a Small Craft Advisory for the outer waters from San Mateo Point to the Mexican border (10 to 60 miles out, including San Clemente Island) from 10 AM Wednesday to 10 AM Thursday, with seas falling below 10 feet by Thursday evening.
watch_for: Thursday morning's high tide, when locally extreme coastal flooding is expected on top of 6–8 foot surf

confidence: The warm, breezy stretch through Friday and the weekend cooling are presented without major doubts, but confidence is lower in the timing, track and details of next week's storms.
